activities.anchor: The uncomfortable finding that shapes the whole discipline
activities.caption: file each failure by the phase it lives in
activities.name: mlsPhaseBuckets

config.prompt: Three phases, three sets of enemies — file each failure:

items.label: wrong patient — a label applied later, from memory
a needle traversing the vein's wall
a specimen left on a sunny windowsill
an uncalibrated analyser, tightly clustered but offset
instrument drift from an aging reagent lot
a critical value that reached a screen but never a clinician's ears
a transcription slip between analyser and record

config.why: Around 60–70 per cent of laboratory errors are pre-analytical, most at collection — the specimen is not the result's raw material; it is the result.

activities.anchor: an order designed so that each tube
activities.caption: rebuild the order of draw
activities.name: mlsDrawOrder

config.prompt: The order of draw — drag the tubes into their sequence:
items: Blood culture bottles — sterility above all
config.why: Each additive does a job — citrate binds calcium reversibly, EDTA chelates it irreversibly, fluoride stops cells consuming glucose — and the sequence keeps one tube's chemistry out of the next.

activities.anchor: Before it ever reaches the chart
activities.caption: walk the 3 am critical-value decision
activities.name: mlsPotassiumBranch

config.root: 3 am. A potassium of 6.8 mmol/L — well into the critical range — comes off the analyser. Yesterday's potassium: 4.1. The haemolysis index reads gross.

start.text: Autoverification has blocked release. What happens next?

choices.label: Call the ward and request a repeat specimen
choices.feedback: The delta check and the haemolysis index both fired — the system is shouting for a reason.

choices.label: Release it — the analyser reported a number
choices.feedback: A number is not yet an answer.

repeat.text: The repeat, drawn gently, reports 4.3 mmol/L. The first result was never true — it was an artefact with the power to trigger urgent treatment.

release.text: Released, the fabricated hyperkalaemia would drive treatment on the strength of ruptured cells. The machinery exists to stop exactly this.

config.why: Delta checks, haemolysis indices and critical-value call-backs are what convert a number into a trustworthy answer.

activities.caption: pair each QC instrument with its job
activities.name: mlsQualityMatch

config.prompt: The quality vocabulary — pair each term with its work:

pairs.right: closeness of repeated values to one another
anchors the instrument to reference material of known value — defining where "true" is
known-value specimens run exactly like patient samples, policed run by run

config.why: A machine in control scatters its dots randomly around the mean; drift announces itself as a slow walk upward long before results go wrong.

activities.anchor: system is the accepted grammar for reading the chart
activities.caption: file each Westgard pattern by its verdict
activities.name: mlsWestgardBuckets

config.prompt: Warning or rejection? File each pattern:

items.label: two consecutive points beyond the same 2 SD line (2-2s)
four consecutive points beyond the same 1 SD line (4-1s)
ten consecutive points on one side of the mean (10x)

config.why: The question is never "does the machine look fine?" but "could this pattern of deviations arise by chance alone?" — only randomness earns a release stamp.

activities.anchor: ISO 15189 is the international laboratory standard
activities.caption: fill the blanks — control versus assurance
activities.name: mlsQcQaCloze

config.text: Quality %%0%% is the daily machinery of detection; quality %%1%% is the system that guarantees the machinery is running, staff are competent and processes improve.
config.hint: One is what you run every shift; the other is the programme standing around it.

activities.anchor: a calculation performed daily in reagent preparation
activities.caption: drop the marker on the stock volume
activities.name: mlsSalinePlace

config.prompt: You need 500 mL of 0.85% saline from a 9% stock. Place the marker on the volume of stock to measure out, before making up to volume:
config.why: (0.85 × 500) ⁄ 9 ≈ 47 mL, made up to 500 mL — C₁V₁ = C₂V₂, the bench's daily bread.
